Title: Monthly Stock Sector Outlook (2026) | Charles Schwab
# Sector Views: Monthly Stock Sector Outlook. Our outlook on the 11 S&P 500 equity sectors. *Schwab Sector Views is our six- to 12-month outlook for stock sectors, which represent broad sectors of the economy. The Schwab Center for Financial Research (SCFR) combines a factor-based approach with a market and economic assessment to determine the ratings. For the basics on sectors, please see**Stock Sectors: What Are They? Beginning in March 2026, we've expanded our sector ratings to five levels: Most Favored, More Favored, Neutral, Less Favored, and Least Favored. See the "How Should I Use Sector Views?" section for more information. **Industrials** should benefit from increased capital spending in key growth areas like electricity capacity, construction around the artificial intelligence-related (AI) infrastructure buildout, defense, and energy, which also supports **Materials**. The **Energy** sector has outperformed since the start of the Iran war with high oil prices driving earnings upgrades. **Consumer Discretionary** fundamentals have weakened recently with softer revenue and free-cash-flow trends relative to other sectors (free cash flow is the amount of cash a company has left after spending on operations and capital asset maintenance). Sector ratings on a five-point scale: least favored, less favored, neutral, more favored, and most favored. Communications Services is more favored. Consumer Discretionary is least favored. Consumer Staples is less favored. Health Care is most favored. Industrials is most more favored. Real Estate is least favored. The ratings Most Favored, More Favored, Neutral, Less Favored and Least Favored reflect SCFR's opinions about the likelihood that the sector will perform better (Most Favored, More Favored), about the same (Neutral), or worse (Less Favored, Least Favored) than the broader S&P 500® index during the next six to 12 months. ### Communication Services sector (rating: More Favored). **Risks:** Communication Services has a high exposure to advertising, which can be pressured during periods of economic slowdown. ### Consumer Discretionary sector (rating: Least Favored). ### Consumer Staples sector (rating: Less Favored). ### Health Care sector (rating: Most Favored). ### Industrials sector (rating: More Favored). ### Materials sector (rating: More Favored). The views are positioned across a five-point spectrum: Least Favored, Less Favored, Neutral, More Favored, and Most Favored.

Monthly Stock Sector Outlook (2026) | Charles Schwab. ### Sector ratings. ### Communication Services sector (rating: Outperform). ### Consumer Discretionary sector (rating: Underperform). ### Consumer Staples sector (rating: Marketperform). ### Financials sector (rating: Marketperform). ### Information Technology sector (rating: Marketperform). **Positives:** The Utilities sector has tended to perform relatively better when economic growth slows, as consumers usually cut spending on other items before they stop paying utility bills. The sectors are then evaluated relative to the S&P 500 index to arrive at one of three preliminary ratings: Outperform, Marketperform, and Underperform. Once confirmed, these ratings will reflect our view of how the sector is likely to perform relative to the S&P 500 during the coming six to 12 months. For example, there may be times when the data point toward a rating but SCFR's experts have strong reason to believe that an economic, market, or geopolitical shift is underway that would change the sector outlook. Investors who want to make tactical shifts in their portfolios can use Schwab Sector Views' Outperform, Underperform, and Marketperform ratings as a resource. Investors and clients should consider sectors as only a single factor in making their investment decision while considering the current market environment. **Communication Services sector:**The Communication Services Sector includes telecom and media & entertainment companies including producers of interactive gaming products and companies engaged in content and information creation or distribution through proprietary platforms. **Energy sector:**The Energy sector includes companies that operate in the areas of exploration & production, refining & marketing, and storage & transportation of oil & gas and coal & consumable fuels. **Financials sector:**The Financials sector includes banking, financial services, consumer finance, capital markets and insurance activities. **Health Care sector:**The Health Care sector includes health care providers & services, health care equipment & supplies, and health care technology companies. **Industrials sector:**The Industrials sector includes aerospace & defense, building products, electrical equipment and machinery and companies that offer construction & engineering services. **Information Technology sector:**The Information Technology sector includes software and information technology services, manufacturers and distributors of technology hardware & equipment such as communications equipment, cellular phones, computers & peripherals, electronic equipment and related instruments, and semiconductors and related equipment & materials.

**Investing involves risk, including loss of principal.** ### Factors behind the stock sector ratings Source: Schwab Center for Financial Research, S&P Dow Jones Indices, as of 7/26/2024. The Schwab Center for Financial Research reserves the right to override the Schwab Sector Views Model; see "Sector Views Process" below for an explanation of how SCFR determines its ratings. ### Consumer Discretionary sector (rating: Underperform) **Positives:** Companies tend to be sensitive to economic activity, as consumers buy discretionary items more readily when job growth is strong and interest rates are low. ### Consumer Staples sector (rating: Marketperform) **Positives:** Consumer Staples companies tend to be relatively insensitive to economic activity, as consumers buy staples regardless of economic conditions. ### Energy sector (rating: Outperform) **Positives:** Energy stocks are generally supported by relatively high oil prices. ### Industrials sector (rating: Marketperform) **Positives:** Industrials often benefit when economic growth raises business confidence, resulting in new building projects, machinery purchases, increased airline travel and shipments. ### Information Technology sector (rating: Marketperform) **Positives:** Information Technology tends to do well when strong economic growth encourages companies to invest in technology upgrades and consumers to buy new devices. **Risks:** Many companies in the sector trade at higher multiples (price relative to earnings), and a rising-interest-rate environment puts downward pressure on valuations. ### Real Estate sector (rating: Underperform) **Positives:** Real Estate, which consists primarily of commercial real estate investment trusts (REITs), tends to benefit from economic growth, which supports rent collections and property prices. ### Utilities sector (rating: Marketperform) **Positives:** The Utilities sector has tended to perform relatively better when economic growth slows, as consumers usually cut spending on other items before they stop paying utility bills. The sectors are then evaluated relative to the S&P 500 index to arrive at one of three preliminary ratings: Outperform, Marketperform and Underperform. For example, there may be times when the model points toward a rating based on recent data, but SCFR's experts have strong reason to believe that an economic, market or geopolitical shift is underway that would change the sector outlook. Investors who want to make tactical shifts in their portfolios can use Schwab Sector Views' Outperform, Underperform and Marketperform ratings as a resource.
